task_message:
Case M06: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 440x440x224 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Segmentation complete for case M06.

**Result:** A single connected myxoid soft-tissue tumor in the left posterior perineal/gluteal subcutaneous tissue, T2-hyperintense and lobulated, spanning axial slices 73–137, with a final volume of **66.6 mL**.

**How I got there:**
- `seg_open` + axial/sagittal/coronal contact sheets localized the bright lobulated mass in the left posterior subcutaneous fat, well away from bone marrow, bladder, bowel and the central perineal organs.
- One positive point prompt at the lesion core (mark 1208, axial 105) produced a clean single-component mask.
- Verified the boundary at the core (axial 80/85/105, sagittal 163/184, coronal 156) and at both poles (axial 65/128/145), plus bilateral comparison to exclude normal fascial/vascular hyperintensity.
- Checked automatic candidates: C1/C2 were the body's subcutaneous fat ring, C3 a dilated normal-fat shell — all rejected.

Confidence is **medium** rather than high only because the most superior pole of the tumor fades gradually into adjacent tissue, making that margin slightly less crisp; the rest of the outline follows the lesion edge clearly in all three planes.
